extra.message: Request body is passed directly to pickle.loads() which allows arbitrary code execution. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload that executes code upon deserialization.
Query parameter 'host' is concatenated directly into os.system() call. An attacker can inject shell commands via the host parameter, e.g., '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd'.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command (OS Command Injection)

extra.message: XML parser is configured with resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. User-supplied XML body can contain external entity references to read local files or perform SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'origin' header value is echoed back in JSON response and set as an unvalidated CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. An attacker can control this header to inject any cross-origin resource on behalf of the server.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS)

extra.message: Query parameter 'lane' is used directly in RedirectResponse without validation. An attacker can craft a link to redirect users to any external domain via the /ops/after/dispatch-donecard-081?lane=URL endpoint.

User-controlled 'fragment' query parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string. An attacker can inject Jinja2 template expressions to access Flask/Jinja2 internals and potentially achieve server-side code execution.

cwe: CWE-138: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements

extra.message: User-controlled 'card' query parameter is rendered via Jinja2 Template with |safe filter. While the safe filter prevents auto-execution, the value still reflects attacker input directly into HTML response body.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS)

extra.message: Hardcoded demo password 'DemoPass123!' is used for all seeded accounts (admin, dispatcher, workers). This password grants access to production environments where seed data persists.

Hardcoded API key 'fd_demo_status_key_please_rotate' is inserted as a valid integration API key into the database. Any attacker can use this key to call /api/integrations/status-update and modify job statuses.
Database connection string 'postgresql+psycopg://dispatch:dispatch@localhost:5432/field_dispatch' has hardcoded credentials (username/password: dispatch/dispatch) in the default value.
Password reset token is written in plaintext to 'local_mocks/password_resets.log'. This log file exposes active password reset tokens that can be used to hijack user accounts.

cwe: CWE-532: Exposure of Log File Information

extra.message: Password reset token is returned in the API response body as 'dev_reset_token'. This allows interception of sensitive tokens via logs, proxies, or network monitoring.
Seed password is printed to stdout via print statement at application startup. This exposes credentials in system logs, container logs, and process output.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Registration endpoint sets secure=False for session cookie unconditionally in the /api/auth/register response. Cookies should use secure=True in production to only transmit over HTTPS.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in 'Session-Cookie' without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: CORS middleware uses allow_origins='*' and allow_credentials=True with allow_methods=['*'] and allow_headers=['*']. This allows any origin to make authenticated cross-origin requests to all routes.

Password reset endpoint returns the raw reset token in dev_reset_token response when APP_ENV != 'production'. An attacker can send multiple reset requests and correlate which emails return a token, enabling user enumeration.
SSL certificate verification is disabled via ssl._create_unverified_context() for outbound HTTPS requests. This makes the application vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

The 'name' query parameter is used directly as a file path in target.write_bytes(). While pathlib normalizes paths, an attacker could craft '../uploads/etc/passwd' or similar to write arbitrary files.

Mock SSN and credit card numbers (SSN: '111-22-3333', card '4111111111111111') are written to a file in BASE_EXPORT_DIR. These sensitive payment/data identifiers leak into the filesystem and could be exposed if EXPORT_DIR is accessible.
